entries.content: AS001 is a derived analytical series computing the Social Burden Rate. It is constructed from Net Social Wage (NSW, S607) and exploitation-related series. The social burden rate measures the proportion of surplus value absorbed by the net fiscal impact on workers — i.e., taxes paid by workers minus benefits and services received.
entries.verbatim_quote: APPENDIX I: Rates of Exploitation of Productive and Unproductive Workers. Companion text: Section 4.2 (theoretical derivation of relative exploitation rates). Purpose: Calculate and compare rates of exploitation for productive vs. unproductive workers.

entries.content: Registry describes AS001 as 'derived from NSW + exploitation series' with source_type 'analytical'. The legacy construction script is A07_social_burden_rate.py. Units are ratio. The series covers 1948-2024.
entries.verbatim_quote: Main Formula: (1 + eu) / (1 + ep) ≈ (hu/hp) / (ecu/ecp). Where eu = rate of exploitation of unproductive workers; ep = rate of exploitation of productive workers; hu = hours per unproductive worker; hp = hours per productive worker; ecu = employee compensation per unproductive worker; ecp = employee compensation per productive worker.

entries.content: The social burden rate conceptually relates to Chapter 6's analysis of the net social wage (S607 = B_w + G_w - T_w) and its ratio to variable capital or surplus value. AS001 likely computes NSW relative to an exploitation measure (e.g., S*/V* or similar), quantifying the net fiscal redistribution burden on the surplus.
entries.verbatim_quote: Known: ep = S*/V* (rate of surplus value for productive workers). Solve for eu: eu = (hu/hp) / (ecu/ecp) · [1 + S*/V*] - 1.

entries.content: Key input series: S607 (Net Social Wage), plus exploitation/surplus value series from Chapter 5 (e.g., S506 rate of surplus value, S505 surplus value). The construction array in the registry is empty, indicating this was handled by a standalone analytical script rather than the standard pipeline.
entries.verbatim_quote: Table I.1 shows 25 numbered steps for annual calculations 1948-89.

entries.content: Divide equation (1) by utilized capital K*.u: r'n = [1 - T/S* - Eu/S*][S*/(K*.u)] = (1-t-eu)r*' = (1-b)r*'. Where r*' = S*/(K*.u) = capacity utilization-adjusted Marxian rate of profit; r'n = Pn/(K*.u) = similarly adjusted NIPA-based net rate of profit; t = T/S* = tax share of surplus value; eu = Eu/S* = unproductive expenses share of surplus value; b = t + eu = social burden rate.
entries.context: Ch7 §7.1 | AS001 primary definition -- this is the book's verbatim formal definition of the social burden rate b = t + eu, the exact concept AS001 measures. The legacy script name A07_social_burden_rate.py is anchored directly to this equation.

entries.content: Observed net rate of profit r'n will fall relative to Marxian general rate r*' when greater proportion of surplus value absorbed in business taxes or unproductive expenses. Hence: b = social burden rate.
entries.context: Ch7 §7.1 | AS001 interpretive anchor -- the book's own statement of WHY this ratio is called the social burden rate. Justifies AS001's framing as the share-of-surplus-value-absorbed metric, not merely a fiscal ratio.

entries.content: Figure 7.1 shows the corresponding rise of 16% in social burden rate b over postwar period. Figure 7.2 result: NIPA-based rate rn falls substantially faster than Marxian rate. Marxian rate falls 25%, NIPA-based rate falls 39%.
entries.context: Ch7 §7.1 | AS001 empirical anchor -- book's headline numeric finding for the social burden rate (rises 16% over 1948-1989, from ~0.56 to ~0.66). This is the validation target for AS001's book-period values.

entries.content: Net transfer: NT = Benefits received by workers - Taxes paid by workers. Purpose: Measure net impact of state expenditures and taxes on standard of living of wage/salary earners. Finding: Net transfer is negative over most of 1952-85 period -> net tax on workers.
entries.context: Appendix N | AS001 cross-link to S607/S608 NSW component -- AS001's input series include NSW; this is the book's Appendix N definition of the underlying net-transfer concept and its empirical sign (negative throughout the postwar period).

citations.full: Shaikh, Anwar, and E. Ahmet Tonak. 1994. Measuring the Wealth of Nations: The Political Economy of National Accounts. Cambridge University Press.

methodology_summary: Derived analytical ratio measuring the social burden rate, computed from Net Social Wage (S607) and exploitation-related series. Legacy script: A07_social_burden_rate.py.
